days6To15.title: UK Outlook for Saturday 14 Nov 2026 to Monday 23 Nov 2026
days6To15.text: High pressure will initially dominate, with widely settled conditions and overnight frost. Some showers are likely in northern and western Scotland though, and perhaps along some other western coasts for a time. Later in the weekend, a transition to more unsettled conditions is expected as bands of rain, and associated areas of low pressure, arrive from the North Atlantic, bringing more widespread wet and windy weather. It is likely to remain fairly changeable through the remainder of the period, with occasional rain interspersed with brighter, showery spells. Whilst colder conditions will be possible at times, especially at first, it will often be mild, with temperatures near or a little above average for the time of year.

days16To30.title: UK Outlook for Wednesday 25 Nov 2026 to Wednesday 9 Dec 2026
days16To30.text: Changeable or unsettled conditions are expected initially, with Atlantic weather systems bringing spells of rain and strong winds at times, interspersed with brighter, showery periods. Through late November, low pressure may become slower-moving to the west of the UK, potentially bringing more prolonged rainfall, particularly to southern and western areas, along with a continued risk of strong winds. Into December, confidence becomes low, but there is a possibility that low pressure tracks shift further south as high pressure builds to the north. This could bring further rain at times to central and southern areas, while northern parts become somewhat drier. Temperatures will probably be near or slightly above average in the south, with an increasing chance of colder conditions extending southwards from the north into December.

sections.text: Dense fog during the morning giving poor visibilities, lingering in places. Turning cloudier during the afternoon with outbreaks of rain by the evening. Feeling chilly with a breeze.

sections.text: A damp evening for most with outbreaks of rain. Rain continuing throughout the night, becoming lighter and patchier by dawn. Breezy with temperatures above freezing.

sections.title: Wednesday:
sections.text: Cloudy to start with patchy rain through the morning. Turning drier through the morning, bringing some glimmers of sunshine. Chilly with a frost overnight into Thursday.

sections.title: Outlook for Thursday to Saturday:
sections.text: Dry with plenty of autumnal sunshine throughout. Feeling colder, especially in the brisk northerly winds to start with overnight frost. Hazy sunshine for Saturday.

sections.title: Wednesday:
sections.text: Patchy rain and drizzle across the south at first, becoming drier with some brighter moments developing before evening. Frequent blustery showers push into the northeast through the afternoon.

sections.title: Outlook for Thursday to Saturday:
sections.text: Feeling markedly colder over the next few days in northerly winds, with frosty nights. Showery around the coasts, with wintery showers pushing into the far north with strong winds.

days6To15.title: UK Outlook for Saturday 14 Nov 2026 to Monday 23 Nov 2026
days6To15.text: High pressure will initially dominate, with widely settled conditions and overnight frost. Some showers are likely in northern and western Scotland though, and perhaps along some other western coasts for a time. Later in the weekend, a transition to more unsettled conditions is expected as bands of rain, and associated areas of low pressure, arrive from the North Atlantic, bringing more widespread wet and windy weather. It is likely to remain fairly changeable through the remainder of the period, with occasional rain interspersed with brighter, showery spells. Whilst colder conditions will be possible at times, especially at first, it will often be mild, with temperatures near or a little above average for the time of year.

days16To30.title: UK Outlook for Wednesday 25 Nov 2026 to Wednesday 9 Dec 2026
days16To30.text: Changeable or unsettled conditions are expected initially, with Atlantic weather systems bringing spells of rain and strong winds at times, interspersed with brighter, showery periods. Through late November, low pressure may become slower-moving to the west of the UK, potentially bringing more prolonged rainfall, particularly to southern and western areas, along with a continued risk of strong winds. Into December, confidence becomes low, but there is a possibility that low pressure tracks shift further south as high pressure builds to the north. This could bring further rain at times to central and southern areas, while northern parts become somewhat drier. Temperatures will probably be near or slightly above average in the south, with an increasing chance of colder conditions extending southwards from the north into December.
